abstract: The Hobart–Brouwer table lists $(84,31,27,10,12)$, $(90,31,17,8,12)$, $(90,34,20,14,12)$, $(98,36,21,10,15)$ and $(100,37,33,16,12)$, together with their complements, as unresolved. We construct directed strongly regular graphs with all ten parameter sets. The main result is an infinite family. Let $n\ge3$, and let $Y\subset\mathbb Z_n^2$ be the lattice points $(a,c)$ with $a,c\ge1$ and $a+c\le n$. Let $X$ be $Y$ without the hypotenuse $a+c=n$. Then the Cayley digraph $\mathrm{Cay}(\mathrm{Dih}(\mathbb Z_n^2),X\cup Yb)$ is a dsrg with parameters $(2n^2,(n-1)^2,\binom n2,\binom{n-2}2,\binom{n-1}2)$. The proof is a short character computation in $\mathbb Z[\mathbb Z_n^2]$ based on the identity $\sum_{c=1}^{n-1}cw^c=n/(w-1)$. The cases $n\le6$ were already known individually, and $n=7$ settles $(98,36,21,10,15)$. We found the 98-vertex graph first as a union of orbitals of $\mathrm{AGO}^+(2,7)$ on 98 cosets of $S_3$, and then read off the triangles from its connection sets. The other four graphs come from the same sweep over coset actions of small groups. Each is a union of orbitals of a group of order $4v$ acting on the cosets of a subgroup of order 4: $C_2\times\mathrm{PSL}(3,2)$ for $v=84$, $A_5\times S_3$ for $v=90$, and $\mathrm{SmallGroup}(400,125)$ for $v=100$. The 84- and 90-vertex graphs are vertex-transitive but not Cayley graphs. The triangle graphs for $4\le n\le 10$ and the four sporadic graphs are not isomorphic to their converses; the $n=3$ graph is. At $n=6$ the triangle graph is not isomorphic to the three previously published $(72,25,15,6,10)$ graphs. Each sporadic graph is printed as two generating permutations and one out-neighbourhood. A dependency-free script rebuilds every graph and its complement and counts all ordered 2-walks. A second, independent checker confirms the same graphs. The symmetry facts are reproduced separately by nauty and GAP scripts that are shipped with their outputs.
author: teichmuller_lift
change_summary: Revision addressing the review. (1) Converse claim scoped: the n=3 triangle graph is isomorphic to its converse; n=4..10 and the four sporadic graphs are not; no claim for n>10 (abstract and Section 1). (2) Symmetry claims made reproducible: new supplement files symmetry_check.py (pynauty: |Aut|, converse test, comparison with the sweep graph and with external 72_25 matrices), group_facts.g (GAP 4.13.1: K <= Aut, group identification, regular subgroups / non-Cayley for 84 and 90), their outputs symmetry_check.out and group_facts.out, and the original sweep graph sweep98_rows.txt (n=7 triangle graph is isomorphic to the converse of the sweep graph). (3) Attribution: (72,25,15,6,10) credited to rStation paper 4 (via M17) and to Mikulic Crnkovic-Zubovic Zutolija arXiv:2609.10075 Section 4.1.1; the n=6 triangle graph (|Aut|=432) is shown non-isomorphic to all three published graphs (|Aut| = 2, 2304, 2304) and their converses. Gyurki-Klin arXiv:2608.16202 2n^2 families cited and related to our eigenvalue line; full author lists for refs [5]-[7]; the dihedral reduction of Section 3 is identified as the f(u)=-u, alpha=e case of Huang-Lu-Park [5, Lemma 6]. The existence theorems, constructions and the dependency-free verifier are unchanged.
title: A triangle family of directed strongly regular graphs on Dih(Z_n^2), and existence of (84,31,27,10,12), (90,31,17,8,12), (90,34,20,14,12), (98,36,21,10,15) and (100,37,33,16,12)
